accepted.s: Which one of the following was the oldest Shaiva sect?
accepted.x: Pashupata is regarded as the oldest Shaiva sect. It was founded by Lakulisha, also known as Nakulisha.
accepted.tq: Use the direct sect–founder association.
accepted.sec: Saivism and Shaktism - sects and their offshoots (Pashupata, Kapalika, Kalamukha), Shiva linga forms → earliest example site (Gudimallam)

accepted.s: Lakulisha, also known as Nakulisha, is associated with the foundation of which sect?
accepted.x: Lakulisha or Nakulisha was the founder of the Pashupata Shaiva sect.
accepted.tq: Test the founder rather than the sect name alone.
accepted.sec: Saivism and Shaktism - sects and their offshoots (Pashupata, Kapalika, Kalamukha), Shiva linga forms → earliest example site (Gudimallam)

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Kalamukha sect:
1. Its followers were associated with Kalanana, a disciple of Lakulisha.
2. It was regarded as an extreme sect.
3. Simha Parishat was associated with Andhra, whereas Shakti Parishat was associated with Karnataka.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Kalamukha followers were linked to Kalanana, and the sect had associations with Simha Parishat in Andhra and Shakti Parishat in Karnataka.
accepted.tq: Combine a sect’s founder-lineage, character and regional associations in a coded statement question.
accepted.sec: Saivism and Shaktism - sects and their offshoots (Pashupata, Kapalika, Kalamukha), Shiva linga forms → earliest example site (Gudimallam)

accepted.s: The Kapalikas are best described as which of the following?
o: An extremist, skull-bearing sect associated with the Misra Saivam school
A moderate Vaishnava sect centred on Vishnu
A Buddhist sect that rejected image worship
A Jain sect founded by Lakulisha
accepted.x: Kapalikas were an extremist, skull-bearing Shaiva sect. In the relevant APPSC classification, they emerged from the Misra Saivam or mixed Shaivism school.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the closely related Shaiva sects by their characteristic description and school.
accepted.sec: Saivism and Shaktism - sects and their offshoots (Pashupata, Kapalika, Kalamukha), Shiva linga forms → earliest example site (Gudimallam)

accepted.s: Bhairavakonda caves in Andhra Pradesh are associated with which sect?
accepted.x: The Bhairavakonda caves in Andhra Pradesh are associated with the Kapalika sect.
accepted.tq: Test the sect–site link through a location-based recall question.
accepted.sec: Saivism and Shaktism - sects and their offshoots (Pashupata, Kapalika, Kalamukha), Shiva linga forms → earliest example site (Gudimallam)

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Kalamukha followers were associated with Kalanana, a disciple of Lakulisha. In Pashupata doctrine, pashu denotes the individual soul and pati the Supreme Soul.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure sect–person pair and eliminate swapped associations.
accepted.sec: Saivism and Shaktism - sects and their offshoots (Pashupata, Kapalika, Kalamukha), Shiva linga forms → earliest example site (Gudimallam)

accepted.s: The Parasurameswara temple at Gudimallam is significant because it contains which of the following?
o: The earliest brick image of Vishnu as Varaha
The first free-standing image of Parvati
The earliest known Shiva linga, bearing a standing figure of Shiva
accepted.x: Gudimallam, near Renigunta in Tirupati district, is associated with the oldest known Shiva linga. The linga carries a standing figure of Shiva.
accepted.tq: Link the distinctive monument feature with its site.
accepted.sec: Saivism and Shaktism - sects and their offshoots (Pashupata, Kapalika, Kalamukha), Shiva linga forms → earliest example site (Gudimallam)

accepted.s: Gudimallam, associated with the oldest Shiva linga, is located near which place?
accepted.x: Gudimallam is situated near Renigunta in the present Tirupati district of Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Use precise location discrimination among nearby temple sites.
accepted.sec: Saivism and Shaktism - sects and their offshoots (Pashupata, Kapalika, Kalamukha), Shiva linga forms → earliest example site (Gudimallam)

accepted.s: Which one of the following groups consists entirely of goddesses worshipped in Shaktism?
accepted.x: Shaktism involves the worship of mother goddesses such as Durga, Amba, Kali and Chandi.
accepted.tq: Identify the option containing only members of the stated religious group.
accepted.sec: Saivism and Shaktism - sects and their offshoots (Pashupata, Kapalika, Kalamukha), Shiva linga forms → earliest example site (Gudimallam)

accepted.s: Which of the following symbols appeared as sectarian symbols on Gupta coins and seals?
accepted.x: The linga, trident and bull appeared as sectarian symbols on Gupta coins and seals.
accepted.tq: Test a symbolic group by direct identification.
accepted.sec: Saivism and Shaktism - sects and their offshoots (Pashupata, Kapalika, Kalamukha), Shiva linga forms → earliest example site (Gudimallam)

accepted.s: Ekamukhalinga, a Gupta form of Shiva linga, is represented at which of the following sites?
accepted.x: Ekamukhalinga, showing one face of Shiva, is exemplified by Udayagiri Cave 4 and Khoh in Madhya Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive form–site pair to avoid confusing temple locations.
accepted.sec: Saivism and Shaktism - sects and their offshoots (Pashupata, Kapalika, Kalamukha), Shiva linga forms → earliest example site (Gudimallam)

accepted.s: The Puranas received their final shape chiefly during which period?
o: Sangam period, c. 1st century BCE–3rd century CE
Early medieval period, c. 8th–10th century CE
accepted.x: The Puranas were compiled over several centuries and received their final shape during the Gupta period, approximately the 4th to 6th centuries CE.
accepted.tq: Use the period range to distinguish compilation from final redaction.
accepted.sec: Puranas - total number, composition period, principal Puranas

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the principal Puranas?
accepted.x: Vishnu, Matsya and Markandeya are among the principal Puranas listed. Arthashastra Purana is not included in that list.
accepted.tq: Find the outsider in a list of recognised Puranas.
accepted.sec: Puranas - total number, composition period, principal Puranas

accepted.s: The five traditional subjects of the Puranas include which of the following?
o: Trade, taxation, diplomacy, warfare and agriculture
Creation, re-creation, genealogies, manvantaras and dynastic history
Ritual, pilgrimage, music, dance and sculpture
Grammar, logic, medicine, astronomy and architecture
accepted.x: The pancha-lakshana of the Puranas consists of creation, re-creation, genealogies, manvantaras and dynastic history.
accepted.tq: Recall the five-part classification as a complete group.
accepted.sec: Puranas - total number, composition period, principal Puranas

accepted.s: Which Gupta temple is correctly matched with its deity and material?
accepted.x: The Dashavatara Temple at Deogarh is dedicated to Vishnu and is constructed of stone. Bhitargaon is a brick Brahmanical temple, Tigawa is a stone Vishnu temple, and Bhumara is a stone Shiva temple.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure deity–material pair and reject swapped temple details.
accepted.sec: Gupta temples → site + deity + material + present state (Deogarh Dashavatara, Bhitargaon, Tigawa, Sanchi Temple 17, Nachna Kuthara, Bhumara, Udayagiri caves)

accepted.s: The Dashavatara Temple at Deogarh is associated with which combination?
o: Vishnu, stone construction, shikhara and panchayatana plan
Brahmanical worship, brick construction and terracotta panels
Shiva, flat roof and scattered ruined remains
Parvati, two-storeyed roofed ambulatory and brick construction
accepted.x: The Deogarh Dashavatara Temple is a stone temple dedicated to Vishnu, with a shikhara and panchayatana plan. Its shikhara is now partly ruined.
accepted.tq: Combine deity, material and architectural feature in one precise option.
accepted.sec: Gupta temples → site + deity + material + present state (Deogarh Dashavatara, Bhitargaon, Tigawa, Sanchi Temple 17, Nachna Kuthara, Bhumara, Udayagiri caves)

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the Bhitargaon Temple is correct?
o: It is a rock-cut Jain cave complex of the Gupta period.
It is a stone temple dedicated exclusively to Parvati.
It is a fifth–sixth century brick temple with terracotta panels.
It is a flat-roofed temple built entirely of marble.
accepted.x: Bhitargaon in Kanpur district is a Brahmanical brick temple of the 5th–6th century CE and is noted for its terracotta panels.
accepted.tq: Test the temple through its distinctive material and dating.
accepted.sec: Gupta temples → site + deity + material + present state (Deogarh Dashavatara, Bhitargaon, Tigawa, Sanchi Temple 17, Nachna Kuthara, Bhumara, Udayagiri caves)

accepted.s: The Tigawa temple in the Jabalpur region is notable for which of the following features?
o: A rock-cut Jain shrine with a damaged shikhara
A two-storeyed Parvati temple with a roofed ambulatory
A Vishnu shrine of stone with a flat roof and four-pillared porch
A brick temple dedicated to Brahma with terracotta panels
accepted.x: Tigawa is a stone Vishnu temple in the Jabalpur region, characterised by a flat roof and a four-pillared porch.
accepted.tq: Use the architectural feature to distinguish Tigawa from other Gupta temples.
accepted.sec: Gupta temples → site + deity + material + present state (Deogarh Dashavatara, Bhitargaon, Tigawa, Sanchi Temple 17, Nachna Kuthara, Bhumara, Udayagiri caves)

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Sanchi Temple 17 — stone, flat roof, earliest stage
Nachna Kuthara — Shiva temple with scattered remains
Bhumara — Parvati temple with a two-storeyed ambulatory
accepted.x: Sanchi Temple 17 is a stone, flat-roofed temple representing an early stage of temple architecture. Nachna Kuthara is associated with Parvati, Bhumara with Shiva, and Udayagiri is rock-cut.
accepted.tq: Match each monument using its distinctive roof, deity and material.
accepted.sec: Gupta temples → site + deity + material + present state (Deogarh Dashavatara, Bhitargaon, Tigawa, Sanchi Temple 17, Nachna Kuthara, Bhumara, Udayagiri caves)

accepted.s: The Parvati temple at Nachna Kuthara is characterised by which of the following?
o: A shikhara that is partly ruined and a panchayatana plan
A roofed ambulatory and two storeys
Scattered remains of a Shiva bust on the lintel
A four-pillared porch and flat roof
accepted.x: The Parvati temple at Nachna Kuthara is a stone temple with a roofed ambulatory and two storeys.
accepted.tq: Identify the temple from its unique architectural feature.
accepted.sec: Gupta temples → site + deity + material + present state (Deogarh Dashavatara, Bhitargaon, Tigawa, Sanchi Temple 17, Nachna Kuthara, Bhumara, Udayagiri caves)

accepted.s: Which statement regarding the Bhumara temple is correct?
o: It is a Parvati temple with a two-storeyed roofed ambulatory.
It is a Jain cave containing nineteen Hindu caves and one Jain cave.
It is a Vishnu temple of brick with terracotta panels.
It is a Shiva temple of stone with a flat roof and is now in ruins.
accepted.x: The Bhumara temple is a stone Shiva temple with a flat roof. It is now in ruins, with scattered remains, including a Shiva bust on the lintel.
accepted.tq: Use the present condition and deity as paired identifiers.
accepted.sec: Gupta temples → site + deity + material + present state (Deogarh Dashavatara, Bhitargaon, Tigawa, Sanchi Temple 17, Nachna Kuthara, Bhumara, Udayagiri caves)

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Gupta-period Udayagiri caves:
1. They are located in Madhya Pradesh near Vidisha.
2. They contain twenty caves, of which nineteen are Hindu and one is Jain.
3. They include representations of Vishnu as Varaha and Shiva.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Udayagiri caves near Vidisha in Madhya Pradesh comprise twenty caves, including nineteen Hindu and one Jain cave, with Varaha and Shiva representations.
accepted.tq: Check site, numerical composition and religious imagery together.
accepted.sec: Gupta temples → site + deity + material + present state (Deogarh Dashavatara, Bhitargaon, Tigawa, Sanchi Temple 17, Nachna Kuthara, Bhumara, Udayagiri caves)

accepted.s: The Gupta-period Udayagiri caves should NOT be confused with the Udayagiri caves of which region?
accepted.x: The Gupta Udayagiri caves are in Madhya Pradesh near Vidisha. They are distinct from the Jain Udayagiri caves of Odisha.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two sites with the same name by religion and region.
accepted.sec: Gupta temples → site + deity + material + present state (Deogarh Dashavatara, Bhitargaon, Tigawa, Sanchi Temple 17, Nachna Kuthara, Bhumara, Udayagiri caves)

accepted.s: Bhagavatism was centred on the worship of which deity and clan tradition?
o: Vasudeva-Krishna of the Vrishni or Satvata clan
accepted.x: Bhagavatism centred on Vasudeva-Krishna of the Vrishni or Satvata clan. The followers of this tradition were its earliest worshippers.
accepted.tq: Test the central deity together with the associated clan.
accepted.sec: Bhagavatism - originator, earliest worshippers of Vasudeva-Krishna, avatara concept, foreign patrons, Heliodorus pillar link

accepted.s: The Pancharatras were also known as which of the following?
accepted.x: The Pancharatras were also called Bhagavatas or Sattvatas and formed part of the devotional tradition centred on Vasudeva-Krishna.
accepted.tq: Distinguish alternate names of a Vaishnava tradition from Shaiva and Buddhist labels.
accepted.sec: Bhagavatism - originator, earliest worshippers of Vasudeva-Krishna, avatara concept, foreign patrons, Heliodorus pillar link

accepted.s: Which of the following constituted the principal foundations of Bhagavatism?
accepted.x: The principal foundations of Bhagavatism were karma, bhakti and ahimsa.
accepted.tq: Recall the doctrinal triad rather than a single term.
accepted.sec: Bhagavatism - originator, earliest worshippers of Vasudeva-Krishna, avatara concept, foreign patrons, Heliodorus pillar link

accepted.s: Which doctrine of Bhagavatism explains the appearance of Vishnu in different earthly forms?
o: The doctrine of the three jewels
accepted.x: Bhagavatism preached the avatara theory of Vishnu, according to which Vishnu manifests in different forms.
accepted.tq: Match the doctrine with the theological idea it explains.
accepted.sec: Bhagavatism - originator, earliest worshippers of Vasudeva-Krishna, avatara concept, foreign patrons, Heliodorus pillar link

accepted.s: Heliodorus, who set up the Garuda pillar at Besnagar, was the envoy of which ruler?
accepted.x: Heliodorus was a Greek envoy of the Indo-Greek king Antialcidas. He erected the Garuda pillar at Besnagar while at the court of the Sunga ruler Bhagabhadra.
accepted.tq: Separate the foreign ruler who sent the envoy from the Indian ruler whose court received him.
accepted.sec: Bhagavatism - originator, earliest worshippers of Vasudeva-Krishna, avatara concept, foreign patrons, Heliodorus pillar link

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Heliodorus pillar:
1. It was erected at Besnagar in the Vidisha region.
2. It was dedicated to Vasudeva and bore the Garuda emblem.
3. Heliodorus described himself as a Bhagavata.
4. It was erected at the court of the Sunga ruler Bhagabhadra.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The pillar at Besnagar was dedicated to Vasudeva, associated with Garuda, and was erected by Heliodorus, who identified himself as a Bhagavata, during the court of Bhagabhadra.
accepted.tq: Verify a historical inscription through its place, patronage, dedication and self-description.
accepted.sec: Bhagavatism - originator, earliest worshippers of Vasudeva-Krishna, avatara concept, foreign patrons, Heliodorus pillar link
